title: Be Kind, Rewind
voice_direction: Kurt: dry, candid, unhurried; let the numbers land, a half-smile on 'passed', 'be kind, rewind' and the final 'on Netflix', no big sell.
narration: In two thousand, Netflix's founders say they flew to Dallas and offered to sell their company to Blockbuster. For fifty million dollars. [pause] Blockbuster passed. Why so easy? Rewind. [pause] Nineteen seventy-six: JVC puts the first VHS recorder on sale in Japan. Sony's Betamax got there first. But early Betamax tapes held one hour. VHS held two. Enough for a movie. And VHS won. In October nineteen eighty-five, the first Blockbuster opened in Dallas. By two thousand four, there were about nine thousand. [wryly] Friday nights came in plastic cases, with a sticker on the tape: be kind, rewind. Then came the DVD. Thin, light, and cheap to mail. In nineteen ninety-eight, Netflix opened for business: movies by mail. Which brings us back to Dallas. Netflix was losing money fast. Reed Hastings named the price. His co-founder, Marc Randolph, later wrote that Blockbuster's CEO, John Antioco, was struggling not to laugh. Antioco remembers it differently. He says there were never serious talks to buy Netflix. Either way, no deal. In two thousand seven, Netflix started streaming. [pause] In September two thousand ten, Blockbuster filed for bankruptcy. Netflix mailed its last DVD in twenty twenty-three. But in Bend, Oregon, one Blockbuster is still open. And in twenty twenty-one, a documentary about it found a home. [pause] On Netflix.

instagram_caption:
In 2000, Netflix's founders say they flew to Dallas with an offer: Blockbuster could buy their company for $50 million. Blockbuster passed.

Why so easy? Rewind. In 1976 JVC put the first VHS recorder on sale. Sony's Betamax got there first, but early Beta tapes held one hour and VHS held two. VHS won. In October 1985 the first Blockbuster opened in Dallas. By 2004 there were about 9,000.

Then came the DVD: thin, light, cheap to mail. Netflix opened for business in April 1998. At the Dallas meeting, Marc Randolph later wrote, Blockbuster's CEO John Antioco was "struggling not to laugh." Antioco remembers it differently and says there were never serious talks.

Either way, no deal. Netflix started streaming in January 2007. Blockbuster filed for bankruptcy in September 2010. Netflix mailed its last DVD in 2023.

One Blockbuster is still open, in Bend, Oregon. In 2021 a documentary about it found a home: on Netflix.

Be honest: did you rewind your tapes? 👇

facts.claim: In 2000 Netflix's founders (Reed Hastings, Marc Randolph, with CFO Barry McCarthy) met Blockbuster in Dallas and proposed Blockbuster buy Netflix for $50 million; Blockbuster declined. Hastings dates it early 2000; reports of Randolph's book say September 2000, so the script says only '2000'.
facts.source: Reed Hastings & Erin Meyer, No Rules Rules (2020), excerpt (Penguin sample; Marketplace, 8 Sep 2020); Marc Randolph, That Will Never Work (2019), via Inc. and The Independent/Yahoo

facts.claim: Randolph wrote that Antioco was "struggling not to laugh" (Randolph's recollection, not independently confirmed).
facts.source: Marc Randolph, That Will Never Work (2019), quoted by Inc. and The Independent (via Yahoo News)

facts.claim: Netflix was losing money fast in 2000 (Randolph: on track to lose at least $50M that year; they needed a buyout 'fast').
facts.source: Randolph book as excerpted by Built In; InsideHook summary of the Vanity Fair excerpt (18/19 Sep 2019)

facts.claim: Antioco disputes the account: says he was not part of a meeting where a purchase was seriously discussed / there were no serious talks to buy Netflix.
facts.source: Newsweek fact check 'Did Blockbuster Turn Down Chance to Buy Netflix for $50 Million'; Next TV, 'Blockbuster's Famous Netflix 2002 Rebuff? That Didn't Happen, Says Video Chain's Former CEO'

facts.claim: Blockbuster HQ was in Renaissance Tower, Dallas, at the time (Hastings: '27th floor of the Renaissance Tower').
facts.source: Hastings, No Rules Rules excerpt; Blockbuster moved HQ to Renaissance Tower in 1996 (Wikipedia, Blockbuster (retailer))

facts.claim: JVC HR-3300, the first VHS recorder, went on sale in Japan on 31 October 1976 (announced 9 Sep 1976); US HR-3300U followed in 1977.
facts.source: Science Museum Group collection, 'JVC HR-3300 VHS Video Recorder'; Wikipedia, JVC HR-3300

facts.claim: Sony's Beta came first (1975); early Beta recorded about one hour, VHS two hours.
facts.source: IEEE ETHW, 'Milestones: Development of VHS, a World Standard for Home Video Recording, 1976'

facts.claim: First Blockbuster opened in Dallas in October 1985 (History.com/Wikipedia: 19 Oct; Dallas Morning News: 21 Oct). Script says 'October 1985'.
facts.source: HISTORY.com, This Day in History, 19 October; Dallas Morning News (4 Dec 2013)

facts.claim: About 9,000 stores at the 2004 peak (Wikipedia: 9,094 stores, 84,300 employees).
facts.source: Wikipedia, Blockbuster (retailer); Bend Bulletin on The Last Blockbuster ('about 9,000 stores at its peak')

facts.claim: Netflix opened for business on 14 April 1998 with 925 DVD titles (pay-per-rental; subscription from September 1999).
facts.source: Encyclopedia.com, 'Netflix, Inc.'; Wikipedia, Timeline of Netflix

facts.claim: DVD launched in the US in March 1997 (Japan, Nov 1996). Not spoken as a date; supports 'then came the DVD'.
facts.source: Sound & Vision, 'Flashback 1997: The First DVD Players Arrive'; Wikipedia, DVD

facts.claim: Netflix introduced streaming ('Watch Now') on 16 January 2007.
Blockbuster filed for Chapter 11 on 23 September 2010.
Netflix's DVD-by-mail service ended in September 2023.
facts.source: AP, 'Netflix's DVD-by-mail service bows out as its red-and-white envelopes make their final trip' (via Boston.com, 28 Sep 2023)

facts.claim: The Bend, Oregon store (211 NE Revere Ave) became the last Blockbuster on Earth when the Perth, Australia store closed (31 March 2019); last in the US since the Alaska stores closed in July 2018.
facts.source: AP via WLOS, 'Oregon now has last Blockbuster store in the world'; KOMO News

facts.claim: The Bend store is still open (2026 travel guides, Tripadvisor reviews Aug 2026; 2024 closure rumour denied).
facts.source: KOIN, 'The last Blockbuster in Bend isn't closing, despite internet rumors'; Visit Central Oregon

facts.claim: Documentary The Last Blockbuster began streaming on Netflix (US) on 15 March 2021.
facts.source: What's on Netflix; Bend Bulletin, 'In ironic twist, Blockbuster movie comes to Netflix'
